title: Majestic King Cage
reviewNotes: All 32 saved states and captions reviewed; native image 28 establishes the complete seven-piece final cage after Qxa6 at 101s: White Ke7/Nb4 versus Black Ka7/Qa6/Ba8/Nb7/b6. Source Nc6 is actual mate: four flight squares are occupied by Black and Nc6 controls b8. Independent Nxa6/Kxa6 loses. Two branches check four distinct tablebase positions and all three encoded moves. Earlier larger sacrifices remain source context outside exact verification.
transcript: Sometimes a game of chess is won by using your opponent's pieces rather than yours. You see, in this position, it seems like we are just in an even endame. Black does have an extra pawn, but this is not really enough to convert this into an advantage. So, the two players here might agree to a friendly draw, but that would be a massive mistake because white has a way to win this game with an incredible sequence that starts with the brilliant bishop takes A7 check, a full piece sacrifice. But if black takes with the queen, this is simply going to lead to a checkmate like this. And if black ignores the bishop, this is an even faster checkmate with this move. But of course, after the bishop sacrifice, black can take with the king. So what was the point of this sacrifice? Well, white follows up with B6. Another sacrifice. If black decides to go back, there still is a checkmate like this. So, black really has to take this pawn. But now, white is not done and plays very precise knight B4 attacking the queen and asking her where she wants to go. But here, black can play the very resilient queen A4 covering the A6 square that is attacked twice and the C6 square where the knight could jump to give a check. And for a moment here, it seems that black is simply out of the woods. White has sacrificed pieces for nothing. But this is where white uncquirs the second brilliant move with queen to a6 anyway dragging the black queen to a6 and using the black pieces to place the black king in a cage creating a situation in which the last piece that white has is enough to deliver this beautiful smother checkmate. If you love incredible chess, follow me for more.
